oncomop

oncomop is designed to facilitate patient characterisation with OMOP analytical tools that follow a dplyr pipe-based workflow, such as PatientProfiles and CohortCharacteristics. It determines cancer stage in cohorts using UICC guidelines.

To install the package, use renv or remotes:


# install.packages("renv")
renv::install("mi-erasmusmc/oncomop")

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mi-erasmusmc/oncomop")

Create a cancer cohort

oncomop derives a stage using the intersection of T, N, and M concept sets. The example below derives the clinical eighth-edition stage for a breast-cancer cohort.

Use CDMConnector to create a reference to an OMOP database and generate a cancer cohort as input to the oncomop package:

cdm$breast_cancer <- omopgenerics::newCodelist(
  list(breast_cancer = 4308306L), # Infiltrating ductal carcinoma
  cdm = cdm
) |>
  CohortConstructor::conceptCohort(
    cdm = cdm,
    conceptSet = _,
    name = "breast_cancer"
  )
#> # A tibble: 3 x 4
#>   cohort_definition_id subject_id cohort_start_date cohort_end_date
#>                  <int>      <int> <date>            <date>
#> 1                    1          1 2020-01-15        2023-12-31
#> 2                    1          2 2021-06-20        2023-12-31
#> 3                    1          3 2022-09-10        2023-12-31

Derive the stage for each record in the cohort

Execute oncomop::addStages() and set showIntersect = TRUE to display the columns containing the T, N, and M date intersections:

cdm$breast_cancer |>
  oncomop::addStages(
    cdm = cdm,
    cancer = "breast",
    window = list(c(-7, 60)), # Search from 7 days before to 60 days after the index date
    edition = "8th",
    type = "clinical",
    order = "last",
    showIntersect = TRUE
  )
#> # A tibble: 3 x 13
#>   cohort_definition_id subject_id cohort_start_date cohort_end_date t1         t1mi       t4d        n0         n1         n3a        m0         m1         cancer_stage
#>                  <int>      <int> <date>            <date>         <date>     <date>     <date>     <date>     <date>     <date>     <date>     <date>     <chr>
#> 1                    1          1 2020-01-15        2023-12-31     2020-01-15 NA         NA         2020-01-15 NA         NA         2020-01-15 NA         IA
#> 2                    1          2 2021-06-20        2023-12-31     NA         2021-06-20 NA         NA         NA         2021-06-20 2021-06-20 NA         IIIC
#> 3                    1          3 2022-09-10        2023-12-31     NA         NA         2022-09-10 NA         2022-09-10 NA         NA         2022-09-10 IV

Return the cancer stage only

If showIntersect = FALSE, oncomop will add a single cancer_stage column:

cdm$breast_cancer |>
  oncomop::addStages(
    cdm = cdm,
    cancer = "breast",
    window = list(c(-7, 60)), # Search from 7 days before to 60 days after the index date
    edition = "8th",
    type = "clinical",
    order = "last"
  )

The result is the original cohort with a derived cancer_stage column:

#> # A tibble: 3 x 5
#>   cohort_definition_id subject_id cohort_start_date cohort_end_date cancer_stage
#>                  <int>      <int> <date>            <date>          <chr>
#> 1                    1          1 2020-01-15        2023-12-31      IA
#> 2                    1          2 2021-06-20        2023-12-31      IIIC
#> 3                    1          3 2022-09-10        2023-12-31      IV

The rules

oncomop includes a set of predefined, UICC-based rules for eight cancer types. Call oncomop::ruleset() to inspect the available rules.


oncomop::ruleset(
  cancer = "breast",
  edition = "9th",
  type = "clinical"
  )
